events.title: The Battle of Mohács
events.shortBlurb: The Ottoman victory that broke the kingdom of Hungary and opened Central Europe to Turkish advance…
body: On 29 August 1526, on the plain of Mohács beside the Danube, some twenty-six thousand Hungarians under the twenty-year-old King Louis II faced the far greater host of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. The Hungarian charge shattered on the Ottoman artillery and the volleys of the janissaries, and within two hours the royal army was annihilated; among the dead were twenty-eight barons and seven prelates.

The commander-in-chief, Pál Tomori, archbishop of Kalocsa, fell with his men, and with him László Szalkai, archbishop of Esztergom. The king, fleeing the field through the evening rain, was thrown from his horse and drowned in the flooded Csele stream. He left no heir, and the broken kingdom elected two rival kings: John Zápolya, voivode of Transylvania, and Ferdinand of Habsburg.

Suleiman entered Buda unopposed and burned it, carrying off its treasures; the Turks returned to hold it in 1541, and Hungary lay split for a century and a half between the Ottoman plain, the Habsburg borderland, and vassal Transylvania. The medieval kingdom that had stood as Christendom's eastern bulwark was gone, and three years after Mohács the sultan's army stood before Vienna itself.
